title: Micro-timings & KV-cache-delta telemetry pipeline for per-token cost attribution
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add end-to-end telemetry that attributes latency and cost at the token level, including explicit attribution of KV-cache hit/miss deltas. This ticket delivers runtime instrumentation, an ingest/transformation pipeline, storage for analytical queries, and dashboards/alerts for regressions. Goal: actionable per-token breakdowns without degrading production latency beyond 2%.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime emits token-level timing events with required fields for >=95% of production requests when flag enabled
Ingest pipeline consumes events and writes aggregated histograms to Prometheus and raw rows to ClickHouse/BigQuery for ad-hoc analysis
Grafana dashboards show 95th/median per-token latency, cache-hit delta contribution, and per-model cost attribution
End-to-end test demonstrating <=2% median latency overhead when telemetry enabled at 10% traffic
Rollout runbook and feature flag to safely enable/disable telemetry; canary at 5% then 25% then 100%
implementation_notes: Instrumentation design: emit lightweight token events keyed by request_id and batch_id. Each event should be a single-line JSON to keep log ingestion efficient. Use OTel span + attribute model where a Request span (parent) contains child spans for kernel_exec and kv_lookup and an emitted 'token_timing' event for decode timing if needed. Data pipeline: logs -> Kafka -> Flink (transform & dedupe) -> write to ClickHouse for raw and to Prometheus via pushgateway for aggregated histograms. Sampling strategy: 1) deterministic reservoir sampling per request to keep tail visibility; 2) full capture for canary customers and test buckets. Privacy: strip PII and prompt text by hashing allowed prefixes; do not store user-supplied prompt free text in token events. Performance budget: instrumentation must add <50us per-token in path or move to async write with best-effort flushing.
pipeline_flow: runtime: emit token_timing events via fast UDP/HTTP local buffer (binary + minimal JSON)
streaming: Flink job aggregates per-request and joins with cache events to compute cache-delta attribution
storage: raw rows -> ClickHouse (hot) / BigQuery (cold), aggregations -> Prometheus histograms for alerting
visualization: Grafana dashboards + Jaeger traces linked by request_id for dive-in troubleshooting
tradeoffs: Raw per-token events blow up cardinality; use sampling + aggregation to control storage costs
Sync vs async emit: sync gives accuracy but risks latency; prefer async batching with bounded buffer and 'best-effort' guarantees
Storing prompt text vs hashes: we will hash prompt prefixes to enable bucketed analysis while avoiding PII exposure
Retention: raw rows 7 days hot, 90 days cold; aggregated metrics longer (1 year) for trend analysis
rollout_plan: Internal canary: enable for infra team traffic (1%) and the integration test suite
Staged canary: 5% production -> 25% -> 100% with monitoring of added latency and Kafka consumer lag
Failover: instant kill switch and auto-migration to sampling=0 if Kafka backlog > 10M or observed p99 latency bump > 5%
Post-rollout: run cost analysis and consider turning on adaptive sampling by model and sequence length

open_questions: What is the long-term retention budget for raw token rows for enterprise customers who request longer auditing?
Should we gate full-capture on 'dedicated' or 'private' customers by default?
Do we want to attribute cost per token using model-specific token-cost rates or a global effective rate?
